title: Messages taking up space on Mac (delete large attachments, or shorten Keep messages)
short_title: Messages using gigabytes on your Mac? Delete the big attachments

verify.notes: Run 2026-11-16 on the recording Mac (macOS 27.0.1), read-only du; nothing was changed or deleted. Apple, 'Change General settings in Messages on Mac' (icht20001, read 2026-11-16): 'To change these settings, choose Messages > Settings, then click General'; with 30 Days 'your conversations (and all attachments) are available in Messages for 30 days', then automatically removed. Apple, 'Delete messages and conversations in Messages on Mac' (icht1035): 'deleting a message or conversation on your Mac deletes it from all your devices where Messages in iCloud is on'; 'If you choose an option other than Forever, your conversations (including all attachments) are automatically removed'; deleted items go to Recently Deleted and are removed from all devices after 30 days. Apple Community 253623827: Messages taking 15 GB on a MacBook Pro; reply: with Messages in iCloud a delete removes it everywhere. 251612366: 12 GB of attachments on a MacBook Air. Legroom claims are from its page: Space Map draws a folder or a whole disk as rings, folders it could not read are drawn hatched, and nothing is removed until you preview and approve. The video does not say Legroom knows Messages specifically. icht1035 'Delete multiple attachments of the same type': select a conversation, click the contact or group icon, scroll to a category such as Photos, click Show more, Shift-click items, Control-click, Delete; deleted items stay in Recently Deleted up to 30 days, removable sooner under View > Recently Deleted. The du run needs Full Disk Access for Terminal (~/Library/Messages is privacy-protected); the video says so. The Storage settings Info path was dropped because Apple's page does not say Messages has an Info button.

scenes.title: Messages is taking up space
scenes.sub: Photos and videos you were sent stay on the Mac.
scenes.narration: If Messages is using gigabytes of space on your Mac, the cause is usually attachments. Here is how to cut it down safely.

scenes.label: Terminal, with Full Disk Access
scenes.narration: On this Mac, the Attachments folder inside Messages holds 4 point 4 gigabytes. Terminal can only read this folder when it has Full Disk Access.

scenes.text: Messages keeps conversations, and every attachment in them, forever unless you choose a shorter time.
scenes.narration: Unless you change it, Messages keeps every conversation, and every attachment in it, with no end date. Years of photos and videos add up.

scenes.label: Delete the big attachments
lines: View > Recently Deleted to free it now
scenes.ui: With Messages in iCloud on, deletes on the Mac also delete on your other devices.
scenes.narration: Save anything you want first: with Messages in iCloud on, deletes reach your other devices too. Open a conversation, click the contact icon, and scroll to Photos. Click Show more, select items, and delete them. Empty Recently Deleted from the View menu to free the space now. Keep messages, in Settings, General, removes whole conversations after a set time.

scenes.name: Legroom
scenes.line: Space Map draws a folder or your whole disk as rings. Folders it cannot read are drawn hatched.
scenes.narration: Legroom is a menu bar app for Mac disk space. Its Space Map draws a folder, or your whole disk, as rings, so the biggest folders stand out. Folders it cannot read are drawn hatched, never passed off as empty. Nothing is removed until you have seen a preview and approved it. There is a free seven day trial.
